### Script for Analysis of CyCIF tonsil dataset for "Are low-variance Principal Components of single-cell omics data biologically meaningful, or just noise?" 
### Reorders Tonsil B channels to match Tonsil A
### inputs: dataTONSILB.csv 
### outputs: dataTONSILB_reordered.csv

### Data source. 
#https://elifesciences.org/articles/31657#content

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{r}
### Load tonsil B data.
tonsilB <- read.csv("Data/dataTONSILB.csv", check.names = FALSE)



### Tonsils A and B were stained with the same antibody panels but imaged in different cycle orders (see Lin et al. 2018, eLife, Figure 5). https://iiif.elifesciences.org/lax/31657%2Felife-31657-fig5-v3.tif/full/1500,/0/default.jpg
### This remapping reassigns Tonsil B's columns so that cycle N in both Tonsils corresponds to the same antibody target.


### Mapping from standardized cycle number to source cycle in raw Tonsil B.
b_source_for_cycle <- c(
  1,  2,  3,  14,
  15, 9,  7,  13,
  11, 10, 6,  12,
  8,  4,  5,  16
)

### Fluorescence channels measured in each cycle. 
channels <- c("FITC", "Cy3", "Cy5")

### Function to reorder Tonsil B cycles to match the Tonsil A antibody order.
reorder_slideB <- function(dfB, channels, b_source_for_cycle) {  
  dfB_fixed <- dfB

  for (ch in channels) {  
    for (cyc in 1:16) { 
      ### Destination slot in corrected data (e.g. FITC_4).
      target_col <- paste0(ch, "_", cyc) 
      ### Where this stain is located in raw B (e.g. FITC_14). 
       source_col <- paste0(ch, "_", b_source_for_cycle[cyc])   
      ### Confirm that all expected source and target columns are present. 
      if (!(target_col %in% names(dfB))) {
        stop(paste("Missing column in Slide B:", target_col))
      }
      if (!(source_col %in% names(dfB))) {
        stop(paste("Missing column in Slide B:", source_col))
      }
      ### Fill the destination column with the corresponding raw Tonsil B cycle.
      dfB_fixed[[target_col]] <- dfB[[source_col]]
    }
  }
  ### Return reordered Tonsil B data.
  dfB_fixed
}
### Reorder Tonsil B cycles to match the Tonsil A antibody order.
tonsilB_fixed <- reorder_slideB(tonsilB, channels, b_source_for_cycle)



### Save output reordered for downstream analysis.
write.csv(tonsilB_fixed, "Data/dataTONSILB_reordered.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
